payload.headline: Micron slips 1.0% to 705.27, just above its 702.02 zero-growth value

summary.thesis: Micron is earning peak-level cash, and at 705.27 the price assumes that cash stays roughly flat. The real question is whether the 74.59% operating margin holds, and the 2026-12-23 report is the next test.
summary.decision: Hold for the long term and wait on a swing trade, because the downtrend has not yet tested support.
summary.act_at: Add at 658.2, trim at 833.11, move to wait on a close below 643.81

payload.happening: MU closed at 705.27, down 1.0%. There was no news, and the stock stays in a downtrend below its 20-day (809.1), 50-day (925.54) and 200-day (769.74) averages. The next earnings report is due 2026-12-23. Options traders hold more puts than calls, with put/call open interest at 2.23.
payload.business: Nothing new has changed the business since the last note. The latest filed quarter (filed 2026-10-09) shows revenue growing 345.03% from a year ago, up from 196.29% two quarters earlier. Gross margin is 80.72% and operating margin is 74.59%, up from 26.14%. Over the past twelve months, free cash flow (cash left after running the business and investing) reached 59.0B, against 1.7B a year earlier. Net cash is 40.6B. The balance sheet is not at risk. What is at risk is the margin: the filings flag that a 75% operating margin is at the top of a 5-year range running from -41% to 75%. Memory chip prices have historically moved in boom-and-bust cycles (general knowledge). Two items move only sentiment or governance. Insiders sold $14.0M outside pre-set trading plans, and the falling price reflects a broad tech downtrend, which the macro read describes as 'fear elevated'. Neither changes demand or cash today.

worth.text: At a 798.0B market value, MU trades at 9.5 times trailing earnings and 6.0 times sales. That is below the 7.9 peer median but at the 70.0 percentile of its own 5-year history. The cash-flow math says the price implies starting free cash flow growth of just 0.1%: in plain words, the market pays for today's 59.0B to roughly continue. Zero growth is worth 702.02 a share and 10% growth is worth 1037.16, at a 10.1% discount rate. The own-history method gives a much lower middle of 490.66 and a high of 833.11, because it uses the sales multiples Micron earned through past cycles, when margins were far thinner. The gap between the methods comes down to one thing: whether peak margins last. The data source does not issue a formal fair-value verdict, because cash flow and sales jumped too much in one year to project forward. So this range is a judgment. The floor is the 702.02 value if cash holds flat, and the ceiling is the 833.11 top of the own-history range.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow stays near today's 59.0B rather than shrinking sharply as the 74.59% operating margin fades from its 5-year peak.

bull: Cash generation changed scale: twelve-month free cash flow is 59.0B, up from 1.7B, and net cash is 40.6B.
The stock is cheap against peers, at 6.0 times sales versus a 7.9 peer median, and 9.5 times trailing earnings.
Growth is speeding up, not slowing: quarterly revenue growth was 345.03% from a year ago, up from 196.29% two quarters ago, with 30.81% growth over the previous quarter.
bear: The 74.59% operating margin sits at the top of a 5-year range that reached as low as -41%. It was 26.14% one year before, and peaks like this usually fade.
The price trend is down, with lower highs and lower lows, and the stock sits below its 20-day (809.1), 50-day (925.54) and 200-day (769.74) averages.

Against its own history the stock is expensive: its price-to-sales ratio is at the 70.0 percentile of the past 5 years, the own-history middle value is 490.66, and insiders sold $14.0M outside pre-set plans.

levels.what: Top of the 643.81–658.2 support zone, which has held twice. It is below the 702.02 zero-growth value, so the price there already allows for some decline in cash. This is the level to add.
Top of the own-history valuation range. Above it, the price depends on peak margins lasting. This is the level to trim.
Bottom of the support zone. A close below it would signal the market doubts the margins, and would move the call from hold to wait.

longterm.why: At 705.27 the price sits at the bottom of the 702.02–833.11 range, and the business has not changed. The downtrend argues against adding before the price tests support at 658.2.

swing.why: The trend is down, and resistance at 730.57–744.96 is less than one 57.56 ATR (average daily range) above the price. The upside is too small for the risk. Enter only if the 643.81–658.2 support holds on a test, or on a close above 744.96.

decision.timing: The 2026-12-23 report falls before the 2027-02-19 options expiry, which prices a 28.1% move, and implied volatility of 109.8 is close to realized volatility of 105.8. New positions before the report carry event risk, and the report's operating margin will likely set the next leg of the price.

change_mind: A close below 643.81 would move the long-term call from hold to wait, because support would be broken while the price trades under the 702.02 zero-growth value.
If the 2026-12-23 report shows operating margin falling back toward the prior 26.14%, cash flow would no longer support the 702.02 floor, and the call would move to avoid.
A close above 744.96, followed by a move through the 803.87–827.58 resistance, would turn the swing call to enter. A move above 833.11 would trigger a trim.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: hold, because the price, now 705.27, still sits at the 702.02 zero-growth value with no news since the last note and the 643.81–658.2 support untested.
